status: registered before execution; benchmark v0 (baselines only, no learned model)
question: G-T2: how well can the single-observation OlmoEarth embedding at an unobserved date be reconstructed from neighbouring single-observation embeddings, as a function of the temporal gap and position?
data: olmo_streaming_dev/single_fp16 (12x768x32x32 per tile, one embedding per kept observation; encoded with synthetic month timestamps, cos ~.989 to real-date encoding per 2026-09-07 probe). Real acquisition dates from sen12_gp_contract via the sealed 12-of-15 selection. Seeded sample of 1500 tiles.
target: single embedding at held-out slot j, j in 1..10 (interior); slot 0 and 11 are extrapolation and reported separately (previous-only baseline)

baselines.linear: time-weighted linear interpolation between j-1 and j+1 using real dates

metrics: token cos (mean over 32x32 tokens) between prediction and target
strata: region prefix of the tile id
reference_ceiling: cos between the two neighbours themselves (how similar consecutive observations already are); a baseline must beat nearest to be meaningful
decision: descriptive. Records the headroom for a learned interpolator: headroom = 1 - cos(linear). G-T4 learned model must beat linear by a bootstrap-CI margin later.
